name: NY-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: Open seat after Velázquez's retirement, but Democratic nominee Valdez heavily funded
Republican Rivera has raised no visible money
Prediction markets price Democratic win near 97%
model.rationale: This Brooklyn/Queens seat carries a +25 Democratic lean, and the Democratic nominee has raised $1.7 million with outside support while the Republican shows no reported fundraising. Markets price a Democratic win around 97%, consistent with a Safe D rating despite the open seat.
model.watch: A surprise low-turnout primary aftermath or an unexpectedly funded Republican campaign could narrow the margin, though a seat flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Nydia Velázquez (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Nydia Velázquez's retirement leaves this heavily Democratic New York City district open, but the seat's fundamentals remain strongly favorable to Democrats. The district's partisan lean of roughly +25 points makes a Republican takeover a steep climb under any plausible national environment.

Democrat Claire Valdez enters the general election with about $1.7 million raised and outside spending on her side, while Republican Melvin Rivera shows no reported fundraising. An independent candidate trails far behind financially. Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97%, and the race draws no attention from expert raters, consistent with a safe Democratic seat.
